adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public member-list endpoint accepts an unbounded caller-controlled limit, allowing one request to materialize and serialize an arbitrarily large group.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb lines 22-23 that `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any caller-provided limit value without an upper bound. This allows an attacker to request an arbitrarily large limit (e.g., limit=1000000), which could cause the server to materialize and serialize a huge number of user records in a single request, leading to denial of service through memory exhaustion or slow responses. This is a security/performance bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — A batch containing valid and unknown usernames silently adds the valid users and returns success, making a partial membership change indistinguishable from full success.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the `add_members` action (lines 63-79), the code iterates through usernames and only adds users that exist (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), silently skipping non-existent usernames. The method then returns `success_json` regardless of whether all, some, or none of the usernames were valid. This means a request with mixed valid/invalid usernames will partially succeed but return the same response as a fully successful request, making it impossible for the caller to know if some users weren't added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — The members endpoint replaces its top-level user array with an unversioned object envelope, breaking existing consumers that iterate the response directly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the members endpoint in groups_controller.rb changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to a new format with `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: {...} }`. This is a breaking API change - existing consumers expecting a direct array of users will now receive an object with 'members' and 'meta' keys. The finding correctly identifies this as a breaking change. However, this appears to be an intentional refactoring to support pagination (adding limit/offset/total metadata), and the corresponding frontend templates were updated (group/members.hbs changed from `each m in model` to `each m in members`). This is a legitimate architectural concern about API compatibility rather than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The members endpoint now defaults to only 50 results for every group, silently truncating lists that previously returned all users for nonautomatic groups and 200 for automatic groups.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is a breaking change that 'silently truncates' results. However, looking at the diff, the old code in groups_controller.rb already had limits - it limited to 200 for automatic groups and had no explicit limit for non-automatic groups (which would use database defaults). The new code adds pagination support with limit/offset parameters and returns metadata (total, limit, offset) so clients can paginate through all results. This is not silent truncation - it's proper pagination with metadata. The frontend code also shows pagination controls were added (next/previous buttons, currentPage/totalPages). This is an intentional API improvement, not a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — Group creation no longer accepts the established nested group payload, so existing callers receive a validation error from an empty name.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the create method changed from reading `params[:group][:name]` to `params[:name]`. Looking at line 24: `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`. If existing API callers send the payload as `{group: {name: 'foo'}}` (the old format), the new code will not find the name at `params[:name]` and will use an empty string, causing validation errors. This is a breaking API change that would cause existing callers to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:37 — Group updates no longer honor the established nested PUT fields or PATCH membership changes, causing existing callers to silently miss updates and potentially clear visibility.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the update method was significantly changed. Previously it handled both PATCH (update_patch for membership changes) and PUT (update_put with nested params[:group] structure). The new update method only accepts flat params (params[:alias_level], params[:visible], params[:name]) instead of the nested params[:group] structure. Any existing API callers sending data in the old nested format (e.g., {group: {name: 'x', visible: 'true'}}) will have their updates silently ignored since the controller now reads params[:visible] directly instead of params[:group][:visible]. This is a breaking API change that could cause silent failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members page now fetches only 50 users but exposes no pagination, so every later member is unreachable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the public members page exposes no pagination, but the diff shows the members endpoint returns pagination metadata (total, limit, offset) in the response at lines 30-35 of groups_controller.rb. The frontend template at group/members.hbs iterates over 'members' which comes from the model that has findMembers() which handles pagination. The public group members page does have pagination support through the offset parameter and metadata returned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — Exact multiples of the page size produce an extra page, allowing navigation to an empty member page.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 13 which contains `totalPages` calculation: `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 users with limit 50), this calculates totalPages as floor(50/50)+1 = 2, but there's actually only 1 page of content. This would allow navigating to page 2 which would be empty. The correct formula should use ceiling division or handle the exact multiple case differently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — Removing the sole member on the last page reloads with the stale offset and leaves the admin on an empty page.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the pagination logic. Looking at the diff, when `removeMember` is called (line 43-50 in group.js), it calls `self.findMembers()` after deletion. The `findMembers` method (lines 23-37) uses `this.get('offset')` which remains unchanged after removal. If a user removes the last member on the last page, the offset stays the same but `user_count` decreases, potentially leaving the user on an empty page since the offset may now exceed the valid range. While `findMembers` does have `Math.min(this.get('user_count'), ...)` to cap the offset, this uses the OLD user_count before the server responds with the updated count. The server returns the new total in `result.meta.total`, but by then the request was already made with the stale offset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — Concurrent page requests blindly overwrite shared pagination state, so out-of-order responses can display the wrong page.

adjudication.rationale: The findMembers function at line 31 makes an async AJAX call and then sets properties (user_count, limit, offset, members) on the model when the response returns. If a user rapidly clicks next/previous pagination buttons, multiple requests can be in flight simultaneously. Since there's no request cancellation or sequencing mechanism, responses can arrive out of order, causing the later-initiated request's response to be overwritten by an earlier-initiated request's response. This is a real race condition bug - the code in the diff shows the next/previous actions call findMembers() without any protection against concurrent requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:12 — Reusing the admin controller without clearing usernames can submit membership text entered for a previously viewed group to the new group.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in admin_group_route.js, the setupController function sets the model but does not clear the 'usernames' property on the controller. Looking at admin-group.js.es6, the controller has 'usernames: null' as a property that is used for adding members. When navigating between different groups, the usernames field from a previous group view would persist because it's never reset in setupController. The addMembers action uses this.get('usernames') to add members, so stale data could be submitted to the wrong group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The caller-controlled limit is not capped, so one members request can materialize and serialize an arbitrarily large group.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 22 of groups_controller.rb: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` - the limit parameter comes directly from user input and is only converted to integer with no upper bound validation. A malicious user could pass an extremely large limit value (e.g., limit=1000000) to force the server to load and serialize an arbitrarily large number of user records, potentially causing memory exhaustion or denial of service. This is a security vulnerability (resource exhaustion) introduced by this code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Adding a batch performs one user lookup per username, creating an unbounded N+1 query path for large membership updates.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the add_members method at line 71 iterates through usernames and performs User.find_by_username for each one individually, which is an N+1 query pattern. This is visible in the diff: 'usernames.split(",").each do |username| if user = User.find_by_username(username)'. While this is a real performance concern for large batches, it's not a bug (the code works correctly) but rather a performance/architecture issue that a reasonable reviewer might flag. The concern is grounded in actual code from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — The add/remove mutation promises do not return the follow-up findMembers promise, so reload failures become unhandled and callers can observe success before the UI is refreshed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, the addMembers function (lines 47-54) shows: `.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` - it calls findMembers() but does not return the promise from findMembers(). Similarly, removeMember (lines 38-45) has the same pattern. This means if findMembers() fails, the error is unhandled, and callers of addMembers/removeMember cannot properly chain on the completion of the member list reload. The finding correctly identifies this as a bug where reload failures become unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — The new add/remove actions discard rejected mutation promises and provide no failure feedback, leaving admins unable to tell that the membership change failed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the `addMembers` action at line 56-60 calls `this.get('model').addMembers(this.get('usernames'))` but does not chain any `.catch()` or error handler. Similarly, `removeMember` at lines 48-54 calls `self.get('model').removeMember(member)` without error handling. The model methods `addMembers` and `removeMember` in group.js return promises from Discourse.ajax calls, but the controller actions don't handle rejection cases. If the AJAX calls fail, the promise rejection is silently ignored with no user feedback. This is a real defect - admins won't know if membership changes failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:37 — Pagination permits concurrent requests without request ordering or an in-flight guard, so a slower earlier response can overwrite the members and offset from a later click.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the pagination actions. Looking at the diff, the 'next' and 'previous' actions (lines 30-47) call `group.findMembers()` which is an async AJAX call. There's no guard against concurrent requests - if a user clicks 'next' multiple times quickly, multiple requests will be in flight simultaneously. The `findMembers` method (in group.js) sets properties including offset and members when the response arrives. A slower earlier request could complete after a faster later request, overwriting the correct state with stale data. The code lacks any request cancellation, in-flight flag, or request ordering mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — No test covers an exact multiple of the 50-member page size, so the floor-plus-one calculation leaves a reachable empty page.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real edge case bug in the pagination logic. Looking at lines 9-13 in admin-group.js.es6, totalPages uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 users with limit 50), this calculates to `Math.floor(50/50) + 1 = 2` pages, but there's actually only 1 page of content. The currentPage calculation at line 6 uses `Math.floor(offset / limit) + 1`, so page 2 would be reachable but empty. The correct formula should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` to avoid this off-by-one error. This is a verifiable logic bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — No request spec covers the new paginated response shape, ordering, metadata, or page boundaries.

The spec file changes (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb) don't include any tests for the GroupsController#members action - only Admin::GroupsController tests are shown. This is a valid concern about missing test coverage for new nontrivial logic that handles pagination boundaries and response shape.
